name: Observations, qualifications and an optional end suggestion
transcript: At eight seconds, her lips keep moving after the dialogue ends. At eighteen seconds, her reaction is hard to read. I don't know how much we can improve that, but the joke doesn't land as well as it could. At thirty-two seconds, Ava's mouth doesn't move during her line. The movement should be subtle, but this line is important. This is a bonus thing. If time allows, stylize the final image at the end and crossfade into live action. This would clarify that the animation is just a short illustration. Overall, it looks great and has lots of charm. One other thing, some dialogue is quiet in the mix. Maybe we can adjust it on our end, but the dialogue should be front and center.

name: Opposite timing directions and negative instructions
transcript: At ten seconds, the door slam lands too early. Move it later to match the door closing. At twenty seconds, the footstep lands too late. Move it earlier to match the foot touching the floor. At thirty seconds, do not show her face looking into camera. Keep this shot on her hands. Overall, the music works well; leave it as it is.

name: Mixed conversation without invented criticism
transcript: At seven seconds, um, the character's mouth keeps moving even though the line is over. My neighbor bought a bicycle and my brother went to the grocery store. Does that sound effect land correctly? It hits too early. It should hit when the creature touches the window. That would make the impact stronger. That's around twenty-two seconds. Overall, the character design looks wonderful.
